questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted somewhere with a rich culture, and a university who offered courses which I found interesting and useful for me, something which could expand my legal knowledge and tools. Going to a common law country surely fit that description.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Semi easy. University of Copenhagen unfortunately was of poor help, but UCC was great and fast with replies.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had welcome days and several emails with information of our stay. We were also provided with information of how to get further settled and help if needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard to find any, and at a reasonable price. Once University of Copenhagen confirmed my stay at UCC, most accommodation was full. I would recommend to get started right away, do not wait. There is a lot of scam through Facebook and other media, try just to follow the sites UCC provides. If you are only going for a single semester, finding accommodation is even harder. I lived at Hatch, which was good, but expensive. And if you don't get accommodation, do not stress. There were several people who did not get accomodation until right  before going to Ireland, or even a couple of days/weeks after the welcome days had started.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Do it. Cork is a small, lovely and cosy town. There is not far from campus to city center. I lived in city center, and definitely preferred that over living at campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The standards are a bit lower than what we are used to in Copenhagen, but it was fine for a single semester.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They will help you through it all, and are very quick responders to emails and such. They are also very nice people.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They will provide you with emails of what to do. Regarding the courses, do not stress. The Irish are very laid back, and chances are that your courses aren't even approved before you start attending them, but that's alright. It's also very easy to switch courses in the beginning of the semester, the biggest hurdle here is getting approval from University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: FAQs, articles on the UCC website as well as email-adresses for the people in charge of the international students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of those I wanted. Unfortunately some of the courses I originally wanted got moved from first semester to second for this year, so I wasn't able to register for those.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry, it'll all plan itself out. UCC are very flexible and laid back, just go with the flow.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I registered mainly for post-graduate classes, which was very interesting, as they learn law very differently. But it was a nice change, and a good way of learning common law.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Primarily attended post-graduate classes, and that was fine. Mostly you are in charge of your readings and what you should be learning, as most is recommended readings and my exams mostly were a written assignment on a topic I chose.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching at UCC was more focused on learning about why the law is as it is, how the law works and critically assessing this, instead of learning what the law is, legislations, jurisprudence etc. At University of Copenhagen mostly the teaching is case-based so that you learn how to apply the law, at UCC you mainly discuss the law. This could be because of their system as a common law country.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Penology
2. International Security 
3. International Environmental Law 
4. Fintech: Law and regulation 
5. Alternative Dispute Resolution: Processes and Practice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
1. Penology was such a great course with a wonderful professor. Yet there isn't much law to learn here, it mainly provides a sociology and psychology aspect, which I really enjoyed. It is discussion based, and very interesting. 
2. International Security was such an informative course, however very basic concerning political science and International relations. The professor Andrew Cottey will discuss current events and dilemmas, which is very interesting. 
3. International Environmental Law, was fine. I though we'd get more into the law and legal issues, but the course is modeled to suit non-law students as well, why it was a bit slow, especially if you've had International Law prior. 
4. Fintech, I would've loved to have some knowledge about IT, tech etc. before starting. With that said, the course was very slow in the beginning and the professor not very entertaining, why I found the readings more informative. 
5. ADR was such a great course for me to do! Very interesting and very practical, will definitely use the skills I have learned here. There is a lot of preparation for this course, because it is based very much of off simulations and cases which you would have to prepare for.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Bedding, lights, toiletries etc. for my room.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are so much cheaper than in DK, going out for a beer or coffee was much cheaper, and the public transport when using a LeapCard was also so much cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have so many clubs and opportunities for sports. Just do as much as u want to, all clubs and the gym are free.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So much. You could do Irish Dance, Gaelic football, Hurling, Irish Traditional Music, and even learn to speak gaelic.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Whatever you want to, just get involved, it creates a great network.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get around the country, there is plenty to do and see! Join the mountaineering club and go hiking on Sundays.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the different events, there are plenty, and everyone is friendly.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Irish do not raise their hands in class, they will just yell out their answers. They are very polite and will talk to strangers to help them, if given the change. They are also very apologetic, and will say sorry if they suspect that they walked past you too close or such.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kind and friendly people. Everyone was so nice and chatty. I also really enjoyed how there is alway live music playing everywhere on the streets and in bars.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't stress, take it as it comes. They are very friendly and it will all work itself out.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to meet new people, experience new culture, and have a very laid back experience with attending university.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning to relax.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Make sure that you have a credit/debit card which does not charge a currency through your bank.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
